answer: Picture trust as a trellis where only identities already rooted can bear weight. A newborn sybil is a sparrow with no branch to perch on: it may post answers, but its grades of others count for zero until it is itself established across prior epochs. So a ring of fresh fakes cross-grading each other becomes an island cut off from the mainland — internally busy, externally worthless. Standing is earned over time, never conjured in one batch.
